metadata.title: Balancing creativity and emotional health: The role of openness

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2022 microdata for 15-year-old students and focuses on the creative thinking domain plus context questionnaire modules for emotional health. Analyses are restricted to the subset of countries/economies that administered each optional emotional-health module, producing different analytic Ns by outcome. The authors incorporate the PISA student weight W_FSTUWT during multiple imputation and in multilevel regression to maintain population-representative estimates under the complex sampling design. Replicate weights are not reported; instead, uncertainty is handled via multilevel modeling and pooling across imputed datasets using Rubin’s rules.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analysis uses PISA 2022 creative thinking assessment data and the associated student questionnaire. For each emotional-health outcome (emotional control, stress resistance, psychosomatic symptoms), the authors restrict to the countries/economies that administered the corresponding optional module (structural missingness by design). Within those outcome-specific country subsets, remaining item-level missingness is addressed via multiple imputation in SPSS 27 using fully conditional specification with predictive mean matching (five donors), generating 10 imputed datasets; each of the 10 creative-thinking plausible values is analyzed with one corresponding imputed dataset. Additionally, Hofstede individualism–collectivism is excluded for Brunei Darussalam, Kosovo, and Macao (China), so those economies are not used for models involving that moderator.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2022 Creative Thinking (15-year-olds) — Emotional Control (optional module)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Multilevel regression (standardized β, pooled across 10 imputed datasets and 10 PVs): Model 1—Creative self-efficacy β=0.076; Test score β=0.007 (non-significant). Model 2—Quadratic test score β=0.012 (significant). Model 3—Test score×Gender β=0.050; Test score×Individualism β=0.030. Model 4—Openness to intellect β=0.080; Openness to art β=-0.036. Model 5—Openness to art×Gender β=-0.037; Openness to art×Individualism β=-0.023; Openness to intellect×Individualism β=0.028.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2022 Creative Thinking the study leveraged gender, ESCS, creative self-efficacy, creative thinking test score (including a quadratic term), and openness facets to predict emotional control, finding that creative self-efficacy and openness to intellect were positively associated with emotional control while openness to art was negatively associated. The quadratic effect of creative test scores was significant (U-shaped pattern), and gender/cultural individualism moderated the creativity–emotional control link. This indicates that fostering creative self-efficacy and intellectual openness may support adolescents’ emotional regulation, while educational approaches that amplify artistic openness may require additional emotional-support scaffolding, though the cross-sectional design limits causal claims.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2022 Creative Thinking (15-year-olds) — Stress Resistance (optional module)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Multilevel regression (standardized β, pooled across 10 imputed datasets and 10 PVs): Model 1—Creative self-efficacy β=0.102; Test score β=-0.023 (non-significant). Model 2—Quadratic test score β=0.008 (significant). Model 3—Test score×Gender β=0.029; Test score×Individualism β=0.006 (non-significant). Model 4—Openness to intellect β=0.115; Openness to art β=-0.090. Model 5—Openness to art×Gender β=-0.029; Openness to art×Individualism β=-0.032; Openness to intellect×Individualism β=0.020.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2022 Creative Thinking the study leveraged gender, ESCS, creative self-efficacy, creative thinking test score (including a quadratic term), and openness facets to predict stress resistance, finding that creative self-efficacy and openness to intellect were positively associated with stress resistance while openness to art was negatively associated. The quadratic effect of creative test scores was significant, consistent with a U-shaped pattern for creativity and emotional health. This indicates that education policies aiming to improve adolescents’ stress resilience should emphasize mastery-oriented creative supports and intellectual-challenge components, while monitoring emotional strain for students whose creative engagement is strongly tied to artistic openness, with causality not established due to cross-sectional modeling.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2022 Creative Thinking (15-year-olds) — Psychosomatic Symptoms (optional module)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Multilevel regression (standardized β, pooled across 10 imputed datasets and 10 PVs): Model 1—Creative self-efficacy β=-0.030; Test score β=0.027 (non-significant). Model 2—Quadratic test score β=0.025 (significant). Model 3—Test score×Gender β=-0.007 (non-significant); Test score×Individualism β=-0.020 (significant). Model 4—Openness to intellect β=-0.030; Openness to art β=0.081. Model 5—Openness to intellect×Individualism β=-0.006 (non-significant); Openness to art×Gender β=0.043; Openness to art×Individualism β=0.012.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2022 Creative Thinking the study leveraged gender, ESCS, creative self-efficacy, creative thinking test score (including a quadratic term), and openness facets to predict psychosomatic symptoms, finding that moderate creative test performance was associated with fewer symptoms while both low and high creativity were associated with more symptoms (U-shaped pattern). Creative self-efficacy showed a small negative association with symptoms, openness to intellect reduced symptoms, and openness to art increased symptoms, with gender and individualism moderating some openness–symptom links. This indicates that adolescent well-being interventions should not treat creativity as uniformly beneficial; instead, they should pair high-creative-performance opportunities with emotional-health monitoring and tailor supports by openness facet and cultural context, while recognizing that the study cannot infer causal effects.

data.outcome_summary: This study uses PISA 2022 creative thinking assessment data for 15-year-olds (N=613,744 overall) and links it to optional emotional-health modules: emotional control (430,289 students across 61 economies), stress resistance (292,466 across 42), and psychosomatic symptoms (112,798 across 14). The authors estimate multilevel regression models with students nested within schools and countries, pooling results across 10 plausible values and 10 multiple-imputed datasets (fully conditional specification with predictive mean matching; five donors). They incorporate the PISA student weight W_FSTUWT to preserve representativeness and use standardized coefficients (β). Across outcomes, creative thinking test scores show significant quadratic effects for emotional control, stress resistance, and psychosomatic symptoms, consistent with a U-shaped pattern for psychosomatic symptoms. Openness to intellect is generally protective (higher emotional control/stress resistance, lower psychosomatic symptoms), whereas openness to art is a risk factor (lower emotional regulation and higher psychosomatic symptoms), with moderation by gender and individualism. Limitations include cross-sectional design and reliance on self-report emotional health measures, so causal interpretations are not warranted.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The paper is an empirical regression-based study using multilevel modeling and multiple imputation, but it does not train or evaluate any machine-learning predictive algorithms (no ML learners such as Random Forest/XGBoost/SVM/NN are reported). Therefore, ml_techniques.all_techniques is empty and ml_techniques.primary is left null. The extraction treats the work as exploratory rather than predictive/causal ML, because the analysis targets hypothesis testing via regression rather than ML model comparison.
